privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Jubilee collects about you, why, who handles it, and how to see, correct or delete it.
privacy.intro: This page explains what personal data Jubilee keeps about you, why, and what you can do about it. It covers the Jubilee website and app.

summary.title: In short
blocks: Today Jubilee keeps only what it needs to run your account: your email address and, if your sign-in provider shares them, your name and profile photo.
What we don't do:

list: sell your data
send anything in your name without your approval
use your data to train AI models

blocks: You can see, correct or delete your data at any time. <contact>Contact us</contact> and we'll do it.

who.title: Who looks after your data
blocks: Jubilee is run by its founder and is not a registered company yet. Until it is, the founder decides how your data is used and is responsible for it (the “data controller” in GDPR terms).
When the company is registered, its legal name and address will be added here, and the date at the top of this page will change.
Jubilee has no data protection officer. For any question about your data, use the <contact>contact page</contact>.

collect.title: What we collect
blocks: When you create an account, we keep:

list: your email address, to sign you in
your name and profile photo, if you sign in with Google or LinkedIn and they share them (to change them, ask through the <contact>contact page</contact>)
when your account was created, last updated and last signed in to

blocks: When you use the site, our host and Supabase record technical data such as your IP address, your browser and the pages requested, to deliver pages, sign you in and protect the service.
Jubilee doesn't collect your resume or your job applications yet, because those features aren't built. Before they are, this page will say what they collect.

why.title: Why we use it

list: To create and run your account and sign you in. Legal basis: the contract between us (GDPR article 6(1)(b)).
To keep the service secure and working. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in protecting Jubilee and its users (GDPR article 6(1)(f)).

blocks: You don't have to give us any data, but we can't create an account without an email address.
We don't use your data for advertising.

processors.title: Who else handles it
blocks: Four companies work for Jubilee to run the service, and only for that:

list: Supabase stores your account and runs sign-in.
Vercel hosts the website and app.
Groq and Anthropic run the AI features (see “AI and automated decisions”).

blocks: If you choose to sign in with Google or LinkedIn, they send us your name, email address and profile photo. They act under their own privacy policies, not for Jubilee.
We don't sell or share your data with anyone else. If we add a provider, this list changes first.

storage.title: Where it is stored
blocks: Supabase stores your account in the European Union (Ireland).
Supabase and Vercel are US companies, so some of your data may be processed in the United States. These transfers are covered by the safeguards in their data processing agreements.

retention.title: How long we keep it
blocks: We keep your account data while your account is open.

Deleting your account deletes your profile with it. Until you can delete your account in the app, ask through the <contact>contact page</contact> and we'll delete it within one month, the time GDPR allows.
Technical logs kept by our host and Supabase are kept for a short time to run and protect the service, then deleted.

rights.title: Your rights
blocks: Wherever you live, you can ask us to:

list: show you the data we hold about you and send you a copy
correct it
delete it
limit how we use it, or object to how we use it
send it to you or to another service in a format a computer can read

blocks: If you live in California, you also have the right to know what we collect, to have it deleted or corrected, and not to be treated differently for using these rights. We don't sell or share personal information, so there is nothing to opt out of.
To use any of these rights, <contact>contact us</contact>. We reply within one month, free of charge.

ai.title: AI and automated decisions
blocks: When you use an AI feature, such as importing your LinkedIn profile or tailoring your resume to a job, Jubilee sends the resume and job text you chose to Groq, which runs open AI models, or, if Groq is unavailable, to Anthropic, which runs the Claude models.
We remove your email address, phone number and street address first. Both process the text in the US and don't use it to train their models.
For each AI request we keep a short record (which feature, its size and its cost), not the text itself, so we can set fair daily limits.

AI only suggests changes, and you accept or reject each one. It never adds experience you don't have, Jubilee makes no automated decisions about you, and nothing is sent to an employer without your approval.

cookies.title: Cookies
blocks: Jubilee sets two kinds of cookies, both needed for the site to work:

list: sign-in cookies, which keep you signed in
a language cookie (NEXT_LOCALE), which remembers the language you choose

blocks: We don't use advertising or analytics cookies, so there is no cookie banner.

children.title: Age limit
blocks: Jubilee is for people aged 16 and over. If you are under 16, please don't create an account. If we learn that someone under 16 has an account, we delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
blocks: When this policy changes, the date at the top changes too. If a change affects how we use your data, for example a new provider or a new purpose, we'll tell you before it takes effect.

complaints.title: Complaints
blocks: If you're unhappy with how we handle your data, <contact>tell us</contact> first and we'll try to put it right.
You can also complain to a data protection authority. In France, that's the <cnil>CNIL</cnil>. Elsewhere in the EU, it's the authority in the country where you live.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.description: The rules for using Jubilee: your account, your content, fair use, and what each of us is responsible for.
terms.intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Jubilee when you use the Jubilee website and app. By signing in, you accept them, so they are written to be read.

summary.title: In short
blocks: Jubilee is free to use today.

list: Your resume and everything you put in Jubilee stay yours.
Jubilee never invents experience, and nothing is sent to an employer without your approval.
You can delete your account at any time.
We tell you before any significant change to these terms.

blocks: Questions? <contact>Contact us</contact>.

who.title: Who we are
blocks: Jubilee is run by its founder from the United States and is not a registered company yet. In these terms, “we” means the founder running Jubilee.
When the company is registered, its legal name and address will be added here, and the date at the top of this page will change.
To reach us, use the <contact>contact page</contact>.

service.title: What Jubilee is today
blocks: Today Jubilee gives you an account that you sign in to with Google, LinkedIn or a code sent to your email.
Jubilee is being built to help you write your resume, tailor it to jobs and keep track of your applications. Before a new feature arrives, these terms will be updated to cover it.

account.title: Your account
blocks: You must be 16 or older to use Jubilee.

list: One account per person, in your own name.
Keep your details accurate.
Keep your email and sign-in accounts secure. Anyone who can read your email can sign in to Jubilee as you.
If you think someone else has used your account, tell us through the <contact>contact page</contact>.

content.title: Your content
blocks: What you put into Jubilee, such as your resume, stays yours.
You allow us to store and process it only to run Jubilee for you, for as long as your account is open. We don't sell it, and we don't use it to train AI models.
How we handle your personal data is explained in our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

ai.title: AI and job applications
blocks: Jubilee doesn't use AI yet. When it does, these rules apply:

list: AI never adds experience, skills or dates you don't have.
You check what it writes before it's used.
Nothing is sent to an employer without your explicit approval.
You are responsible for what you send, so make sure it's true.

fairUse.title: Fair use
blocks: Don't use Jubilee to:

list: put false information about yourself or anyone else in a resume or an application
pretend to be someone else
harass, deceive or harm employers, recruiters or anyone else
break the law or other people's rights, including copyright
copy, scrape or overload the service, or get into parts of it you aren't allowed to

blocks: If we believe content or use breaks these rules, we may remove the content or limit the account. A person looks at each case, we tell you what we did and why, and you can ask us to review it through the <contact>contact page</contact>.

price.title: Price
blocks: Jubilee is free today.
If paid features arrive, we'll show the price clearly before you choose them. We never charge you without your consent.

ending.title: Ending your account
blocks: You can stop using Jubilee and delete your account at any time. Until you can do it in the app, ask through the <contact>contact page</contact> and we'll delete it within one month.
We may suspend or close an account only if it breaks these terms or the law. We'll tell you why, unless the law stops us.

responsibility.title: Our responsibility
blocks: We work to keep Jubilee available and correct, but we can't promise it will always be available or free of errors, or that it will get you a job.
As far as the law allows, we aren't responsible for indirect losses, such as a missed job opportunity.
Nothing in these terms limits the rights you have under the consumer law of the country where you live.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
blocks: When these terms change, the date at the top changes too. Before a significant change takes effect, we'll tell you by email or in the app. If you don't agree, you can delete your account.

law.title: Applicable law
blocks: These terms are governed by the laws of the United States.
If you live in the European Union or another country whose consumer law protects you, you keep the rights that law gives you, and you can bring a claim in the courts where you live.
If something goes wrong, <contact>tell us</contact> first and we'll try to put it right.

contact.hint: How employers reach you. Your name and an email or phone are enough to start.
tips: Use an email address with your name in it.
Your city is enough: no street address.
Add LinkedIn if your profile is up to date.

summary.hint: Two to four lines at the top of your resume. Write it last: it's easier once your experience is down.
tips: Say who you are and what you're looking for.
Name 2 or 3 strengths the job needs.
Leave out "I" and generic words like "motivated".
summary.example: Data analyst with 4 years in retail. I turn sales data into weekly reports managers use, and I'm looking for an analyst role in e-commerce.

work.hint: Your jobs, most recent first. Internships and part-time jobs count.
tips: Start each bullet with a verb: led, built, cut, grew.
Add a number where you have one: what, how, and the result.
Keep each bullet to 1 or 2 lines.
3 to 5 bullets for recent jobs, fewer for older ones.
work.example: Cut monthly reporting time from 3 days to 1 by automating the sales dashboard in Excel.

education.hint: Degrees and training, most recent first.
tips: Put the degree first, then the school.
Add a grade only if it helps you.
List courses when you have little work experience.

skills.hint: Tools and skills the jobs you want ask for.
tips: Use the words job ads use.
Group them if the list gets long: Tools, Languages, Methods.
No bars or ratings: they do not read well in applicant tracking systems.

languages.hint: Languages you speak, with your level.
tips: Use plain levels: native, fluent, intermediate, basic.
List your strongest language first.

projects.hint: Work you did on your own or at school that shows a skill.
tips: Say what you built and why.
Add a link if people can see it.
projects.example: Built a budget app used by 200 students, in React.

certificates.hint: Certifications and licences that matter for the job.
tips: Use the certification's official name.
Add the date you earned it.

awards.hint: Prizes and honours, with who gave them.
tips: Keep it to awards an employer would care about.
awards.example: Best final-year project, University of Yaoundé I · 2022

volunteer.hint: Unpaid work counts, especially when it shows skills the job needs.
tips: Write it like a job: role, organization, dates, results.
volunteer.example: Taught weekly coding classes to 30 secondary-school students.

custom.hint: Anything that does not fit elsewhere: publications, talks, interests.
tips: Give the section a clear heading.
Keep the same layout as your other entries.
